text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: crosslink-az DNS TTL surge affecting PrivateConnect endpoints in az-east-3. Multiple customer connections reporting intermittent resolution failures to privatelink endpoints. Triggered by DNS error rate spike > 25% in az-east-3.

Alice Nguyen: oncall here, I'm looking. Which customers are impacted? ACME reported connection resets and 502s to their API via privatelink.

acme-sre: yes, seeing frequent TCP resets when clients try to connect to privatelink-acme.redwood.net. Happens ~every 10-30s, lasts a few seconds then clears.

Marco Silva: I see DNS query failure spikes from our edge resolvers in az-east-3. Likely TTL churn + zone republish. I can pull dig traces and the resolver logs.

Priya Patel: tagging networking and infra. Paging pd-bot for formal escalation and follow-the-sun handoff if needed.

pd-bot: Escalation created: INC-3632104567. Pager duty notify to oncall rotation in 5m.

Samir Khan: I put a quick note in customer-facing status: "Intermittent DNS resolution errors observed for PrivateConnect endpoints in az-east-3. Engineers investigating." Will update every 15m.

Alice Nguyen: quick checks — running a dig against privatelink-acme from az-east-3 resolver pool:

```
$ dig @10.2.14.8 privatelink-acme.redwood.net +short
10.23.45.67
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
``` 

Alice Nguyen: some queries return address, others timeout. TTLs look short (~30s) in responses when they come back.

Marco Silva: grabbing resolver logs — seeing bursts of SERVFAIL and truncated responses on UDP. Working hypothesis: upstream authoritative cluster rolling redeploy bumped TTLs and caused cache churn + EDNS pathing issues. Also a few signs of packet fragmentation with recent MTU changes on crosslink.

Priya Patel: can you confirm if BGP or route changes happened around the time of spike? I want to rule out routing flaps.

Marco Silva: checked route history — no BGP withdraws in az-east-3 collector for the timeframe. Control-plane looks steady. This is concentrated to authoritative DNS infra and the edge resolvers in that AZ.

Samir Khan: ACME says their internal caching clients are aggressive and retry very quickly which amplifies the issue.

Alice Nguyen: mitigation plan proposal:
- Short term: force authoritative to serve higher TTL (300s) and fall back to TCP for DNS queries from our resolvers to reduce truncation issues.
- Mid term: roll MTU fix on crosslink to avoid fragmentation and validate EDNS sizing.
- Communicate to ACME: ask them to apply client-side retries backoff and confirm no local DNS overrides.

Marco Silva: implementing authoritative TTL bump now. Pushing a change:

```
# rest call to platform-managed DNS
curl -X POST "https://dns-api.internal/v1/zones/privatelink-acme/records/ttl" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"ttl":300}'
```

Marco Silva: also flipping resolver policy to prefer TCP for large answers (netcfg change rolling to 20% of resolvers in az-east-3).

Priya Patel: I'm updating routing and crosslink infra runbook; staging MTU tweak implemented on one spine, monitoring. If that clears fragmentation we'll roll to rest of spines.

acme-sre: thanks — the bump to TTL already reduced churn on our side. Seeing fewer resets but still occasional spikes.

Alice Nguyen: doing health checks for affected endpoints and adding a temporary fallback routing policy for the privatelink VIP to prefer az-east-2 when client latency is within SLA. That should reduce customer impact while DNS stabilizes.

Marco Silva: applied fallback route via smart-router config (canary 10% -> 100% if healthy). Config snippet:

```
route-table set pref-route privatelink-acme {
  primary: az-east-3
  fallback: az-east-2
  policy: client-latency < 80ms
}
```

Alice Nguyen: I ran curl tests through the fallback path; connectivity looks steady. Latency change is negligible for ACME's endpoints.

Samir Khan: updating customer status: "We implemented a DNS TTL increase and temporary routing fallback to reduce impact. Engineers continuing investigation and rolling fixes for resolver fragmentation."

Priya Patel: adding remediation steps to incident timeline and creating a follow-up issue: DNS authoritative deploy gating + improved EDNS testing. Ticket: INFRA-8821.

Marco Silva: opened cloud partner ticket referencing packet fragmentation on crosslink between az-east-3 and backbone. Case #CP-99812.

pd-bot: Oncall handoff scheduled in 2h to next shift (Alice -> Priya). Creating bridge for continuous monitoring.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.internal/bridge/INC-3632104567

Alice Nguyen: handoff notes for Priya: authoritative TTL bumped to 300, resolver TCP preference enabled (canary), MTU fix applied to one spine, fallback route active to az-east-2, customer notified. Watch: DNS error rate and edge resolver truncation metrics for the next 60m.

Priya Patel: thanks — I'll take over. If packet fragmentation persists after rolling MTU change we'll schedule an urgent maintenance window across crosslink spines.

acme-sre: appreciate the fast action. Please keep us posted, we have internal ops on standby.

Samir Khan: I'll keep the status page live and post a postmortem stub once incident is resolved.

Marco Silva: monitoring shows DNS error rate down from 28% -> 4% in az-east-3 after TTL bump and TCP preference. Truncation events reduced by 85%.

Alice Nguyen: marking this as mitigation successful for now. We'll keep bridge open until the next oncall confirms stability. :white_check_mark:

pd-bot: Incident INC-3632104567 moved to "Mitigated". Next update in 1h or on any regression.

Priya Patel: taking postmortem ownership.

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging but bridge will remain open until postmortem. Logs and configs archived under INC-3632104567/artifacts.

Alice Nguyen: thanks team. Low-severity customer impact, ACME ops confirmed they can resume normal traffic. I'll file the after-action and close with runbook updates.

Samir Khan: good job everyone. :thumbsup:
